TX.s01: Array aur Linked List... dono mein data hi store hota hai. Phir interviewer kyun poochta hai, fark kya hai?
TX.s02: Kyunki dono ka data rakhne ka tareeka bilkul alag hai! Chalo cinema hall aur treasure hunt se samajhte hain.
TX.s03: Array matlab cinema hall ki ek row. Saari seats ek ke baad ek, line mein... memory mein bhi bilkul aise hi, continuous.
TX.s04: Seat number pata hai? Seedha wahin pahuncho! Index paanch, ek hi jump mein. Yehi hai O of one access.
TX.s05: Ab Linked List. Ye hai treasure hunt! Har box mein data, aur agle box ka address, yaani pointer.
TX.s06: Boxes memory mein kahin bhi bikhre ho sakte hain. Paanchva box chahiye? Shuru se ek-ek clue follow karo. Yaani, O of N!
TX.s07: Ab aaya twist! Beech mein ek naya dost aa gaya. Toh Array mein? Sabko ek-ek seat khiskna padega. O of N, poori mehnat!
TX.s08: Linked List mein? Bas do arrow badlo, aur naya box jud gaya. Koi shifting nahi!
TX.s09: Toh ek line mein yaad rakho. Array: fast access, fixed size. Linked List: easy insert aur delete, dynamic size.
TX.s10: Padhna zyada hai? Toh Array. Badalna zyada hai? Toh Linked List.
TX.s11: Interview mein ye sawaal pakka aata hai! Reel save karo, aur us dost ko bhejo jo dono ko same samajhta hai.
TX.s12: Aur jaate-jaate, Pretest Passed ko follow karna mat bhoolna!
